sections.h2: What should a seller know about Wyoming, Michigan?
sections.html:
Wyoming is a Kent County city of about 78,600 people that borders Grand Rapids to the northeast, and it is the second most populous city in West Michigan. A seller here deals with the Wyoming Assessor's Office for transfer paperwork, the Kent County Register of Deeds in downtown Grand Rapids for recording, and a handful of city codes that come up when a buyer does an inspection.

This is Wyoming in Kent County, Michigan, and it has no connection to the state of Wyoming. The notes below follow the order of a sale: where the city came from, who buys here, what the city requires, and what gets filed afterward.

sections.h2: How did Wyoming develop into a city of its own?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in 1832 and built mills along Buck Creek, and by 1834 the settlement was known as Little Prairie. The area was organized as Wyoming Township in 1848 after splitting from Byron Township. For most of a century it supplied goods to Grand Rapids, until the Grand Rapids, Holland and Chicago Railway pushed suburban growth.

After Grandville incorporated in 1933 and a General Motors stamping plant opened, Wyoming faced annexation fights with both neighbors and settled them by incorporating as a city in 1959. The 28th Street corridor became a regional shopping strip with Rogers Plaza and Studio 28, then declined in the 1980s, with growth shifting southwest toward RiverTown Crossings. The GM plant closed in 2009, and the city has since worked on the City Center project along 28th Street and the 74-acre former plant site, now called Site 36.

The city covers about 24.7 square miles of land and has 21 parks on roughly 665 acres, plus access to the Kent Trails bike system. The Wyoming Public Library, built in 2002, is owned by the city and run by the Kent District Library. Each year on the last weekend of August, the 28th Street Metro Cruise draws car enthusiasts along a 15 mile route that passes through the city, a regular reminder of how central that corridor is to Wyoming's identity.

sections.h2: What drives the Wyoming housing market?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest local industry, and the 2025 annual financial report names these employers at the top of the list:

  • Gordon Food Service, with 5,000 employees.
  • Metro Health Hospital, with 3,000.
  • GM Components Holdings, with 1,200.
  • ABC Technologies, with 650, and Benteler, with 580.

US-131 runs north to south through the center of the city, M-11 (28th Street) runs west to east, and M-6 skirts the southern edge. The Rapid, the Grand Rapids area transit system, operates eight of its routes inside Wyoming. The Census Bureau puts mean commute time at 21.9 minutes.

Eight school districts touch the city: Wyoming Public Schools in the center, Godwin Heights in the northeast, Godfrey-Lee in the north, Kelloggsville in the southeast, Kentwood south of 56th Street and east of the railroad tracks, Grandville in the southwest, Byron Center near Metro Health, and a small piece in Grand Rapids Public Schools. Confirm the district for the exact address.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Wyoming homeowners?
sections.html:
Wyoming's population is rising. The 2025 estimate of 78,588 residents is 2.7 percent above the 2020 base, and the count was 72,125 in 2010. The 2020 through 2024 figures show 29,417 households averaging 2.61 people, with 67.1 percent of homes owner-occupied.

The median owner-occupied home is valued at $225,200. Median gross rent is $1,196, median household income is $73,677, and 25.5 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Median owner costs are $1,398 a month with a mortgage.

sections.h2: Which Wyoming city rules matter to a seller?
sections.html:
All rental properties in Wyoming must be registered and certified, and the city checks rental status through its BS&A Online portal. An owner selling a rented house should confirm that the certificate is current so a buyer is not handed an open violation. Short-term rentals of 27 days or less must register, which costs nothing and needs no inspection.

The Inspections Department at 1155 28th St. SW, phone 616-530-7285, handles building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits, with homeowners able to apply online without an account. Residential permits are typically obtained in one to two weeks. Property maintenance rules a buyer's inspector may flag include:

  • Grass and weeds kept under 10 inches.
  • Trash containers stored out of sight of the front of the house.
  • Vehicles parked on a paved surface, with inoperable or unlicensed ones stored in a garage.
  • Front-yard fences no higher than 36 inches.

sections.h2: What must be filed with the Wyoming Assessor after a sale?
sections.html:
Wyoming's assessor maintains records on about 25,000 parcels and assesses at 50 percent of the usual selling price. A property's taxable value is capped, so it rises each year by no more than inflation or 5 percent, whichever is less. The cap lifts the year after a sale, when taxable value resets to assessed value.

Every transfer of ownership must be reported on a Property Transfer Affidavit, which the assessor's page says is due within 45 days. Title companies usually supply the form at closing. Skipping it can bring back taxes with penalties and interest from the transfer date.

sections.h2: How is a Wyoming deed recorded in Kent County?
sections.html:
The Kent County Register of Deeds is at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in downtown Grand Rapids. The county's fee schedule lists these charges, payable by cash, check or money order made out to the Register of Deeds:

  • $30 to record a deed, mortgage or other instrument.
  • $5 per deed for the tax certification that warranty deeds and land contracts need from the county treasurer, covering up to 25 parcels.
  • County transfer tax of $1.10 per thousand of consideration.
  • State transfer tax of $7.50 per thousand of consideration.

The county notes that transfer tax is charged on the seller or grantor and that mortgages carry none. The deed must state the total consideration, or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit must be filed, which has no fee. The register's office does not supply blank deeds or give advice on preparing them, so use a title company or attorney.

faqs.q: How soon after a Wyoming sale is the Property Transfer Affidavit due?
faqs.a: It is due within 45 days of the transfer, according to the City of Wyoming Assessor's Office. Title companies normally provide the form at closing, and a late or missing filing can mean back taxes, penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Does my Wyoming property tax bill change after I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, for the buyer. Michigan caps taxable value, and the cap resets to assessed value the year after a sale. Wyoming assesses at 50 percent of the usual selling price.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental certificate to sell a rented house in Wyoming?
faqs.a: The city requires every rental property to be registered and certified, so a landlord should confirm the certificate is current. The Inspections Department at 616-530-7285 can look up the status.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Wyoming house?
faqs.a: Record it with the Kent County Register of Deeds at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in Grand Rapids. The recording fee is $30 per document, and a warranty deed also needs a $5 tax certification from the county treasurer.

faqs.q: When can I still appeal my Wyoming assessment?
faqs.a: After the March Board of Review, the route is the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Residential appeals must be received by July 31, and the July and December boards handle only clerical errors, mutual mistakes and certain exemptions.
